clue.text: Smug company male wanting position not contracted

parts.note: a place is a position
the word 'not' shortened in a contraction such as 'don't' or 'isn't' leaves NT

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied businessman is after a job that doesn't come with a short contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not contracted' is read literally: the word NOT in its contracted form, NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone pleased with themselves and uncritically self-satisfied; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Tactical unit, reportedly essential element

indicators.note: reportedly signals that we want a word said aloud, not written

parts.note: a corps is a military formation, a tactical unit of an army

explanation.surface: A news item about an army unit said to be vital to an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: CORPS is pronounced like the answer: its P and S are silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart or central part of something is its most essential element; a synonym.

clue.text: Muttered brief report of mother's injury

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
bled describes the injury suffered: the mother lost blood

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles a short news item that mother has hurt herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief report of' frames the pieces as a two-word headline, MUM BLED, which run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak indistinctly and quietly is both to mutter and to mumble; a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Bosses releasing man misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in line, so the words releasing man are rearranged

explanation.surface: Managers letting go of an employee who has been behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges the twelve letters of RELEASING MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Line managers are the supervisors directly over a worker, that is, their immediate bosses.

clue.text: Comprehensive booing hard to absorb

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something in, so the word for booing takes the letter for hard inside it

parts.note: a catcall is a jeer or boo from an audience
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Total jeering that is difficult for a performer to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to absorb' puts H inside CATCALL, between the T and the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all term or category covers everything, which is what comprehensive means; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Knight with lots, not complete idiot

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: a word not complete has lost its last letter, here the final S

parts.note: oodles means lots or a great quantity

explanation.surface: A knight with plenty of everything who is still a complete fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not complete' drops the last letter of OODLES, leaving OODLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an informal word for a silly or foolish person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Spy in relationship

definitions.meaning: James ... is the famous fictional secret agent
a tie or connection between people

explanation.surface: An agent involved in a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is Ian Fleming's secret agent; the other is a close attachment linking two people.

clue.text: Not in policy plan

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a line is a policy or official position, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Something that is not part of the official plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough draft or sketch of a scheme, which is a plan.

clue.text: After study I will get crushed and belittled

indicators.note: after places the letter I following the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
grated means ground or shredded into small pieces, crushed

explanation.surface: After working hard someone feels squashed and put down.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to disparage or run down, so denigrated means belittled; a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Maiden in state of collapse thinking

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for maiden goes inside the word for collapse

parts.note: ruination is a state of ruin or collapse
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman brooding while her world falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' is the cricket term, an over with no runs scored, not a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumination is deep or prolonged thought, careful pondering; a noun synonym.

clue.text: Crazy travels to the west creating shock

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftwards, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A madman heading west causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or stagger, to shock; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Penny is such a one!

parts.note: the penny is a unit of British currency; the exclamation hints that Penny could also be a woman's name, so 'such a one' sounds like a remark about her character

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about a woman named Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny is one of the denominations of British currency, a unit of money.

clue.text: Thin goo, no end of it

indicators.note: the word for goo is used with no end, so its final letter is removed

parts.note: slime is sticky goo

explanation.surface: A runny goo, and an endless supply of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of it' takes the last letter, E, off SLIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim and thin both describe a slender build; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Rendering holy greeting when meeting extreme group?

indicators.note: when meeting joins the greeting directly to the group that follows it

parts.note: hallo is a variant spelling of hello, a greeting
a wing is a faction of a party, especially an extreme one such as the far left or right

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a radical faction as if blessing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow is to make sacred or consecrate, so hallowing means making something holy.

clue.text: Frank, taking seat, disturbed those awaiting interview?

parts.note: candid means frank or open

indicators.note: a seat that is disturbed has its letters knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: An outspoken person sits down, unsettling the nervous job applicants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges SEAT into ATES. The question mark flags that interviewees are only one kind of candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Job applicants waiting to be seen are candidates, people under consideration; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Unconventional lady rent with passion

indicators.note: something unconventional departs from the usual order, so the letters of lady rent are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric woman pays her rent with real enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardently means fervently or eagerly, the adverb for doing something with passion.

clue.text: Woman who was beautiful, ace, capital!

parts.note: Helen of Troy, in Greek myth, was the most beautiful woman in the world
A is the abbreviation for ace in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Praise for a woman who was a beauty: first-rate, excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' looks like an old-fashioned exclamation of approval, but it is the definition: Helena is the state capital of Montana.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is the state capital of Montana in the United States, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Hold back soldiers with muscle injury

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a strain is an injury to a muscle from overstretching

explanation.surface: Soldiers held back from fighting by a pulled muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to curb or keep in check, the same as hold back; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bear trapped in river flood

indicators.note: trapped in places the word for bear inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, flowing through Wales, England and Scotland
to lug is to carry or bear something heavy

explanation.surface: A bear caught in a river in full spate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb meaning carry, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or overwhelming downpour of water; a noun synonym.

clue.text: Keep going as one leaving after everyone else

definitions.meaning: to endure or survive to the end
the final person to depart is the last one out

explanation.surface: A determined person stays on to be the final one through the door.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means endure; read as a noun phrase it names the final person to leave.

clue.text: Diplomatic move of Parisian — took steps, getting cut short

parts.note: de is French for 'of', as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, here the last D

parts.note: marched means walked with measured steps

explanation.surface: A French diplomat's initiative, in which someone marched off and was interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cut short' trims the final D from MARCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a formal diplomatic step or representation made to a foreign government; the definition is a near-literal gloss.

clue.text: Fellow children being looked after — they show fear

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning fellow or joint, as in co-worker
wards are children under the care of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: A colleague's foster children turn out to be easily frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: People lacking courage, who flinch from danger, are cowards; a plural noun to match 'they'.

clue.text: Character of body part

definitions.meaning: ... in the old sense means temperament or type, as in 'a man of that ...'
an organ that filters the blood

explanation.surface: A query about the nature of some organ of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an old word for temperament or sort; the other is the internal organ.

clue.text: Raid isn't wrong — time to be seizing property legally

indicators.note: letters gone wrong are out of order, so raid isn't is rearranged

explanation.surface: A defence of a police raid: it is lawful to take goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges RAIDISNT into DISTRAIN, then T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraint is the legal seizure of someone's goods to pay a debt, such as unpaid rent.

clue.text: Disease making one cause to lean back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for cause to lean is read in reverse

parts.note: to sway something is to make it tilt or lean

explanation.surface: An illness that makes a person tilt backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaws is a tropical infectious skin disease caused by a bacterium related to that of syphilis.

clue.text: I would, shortly, being heard and looked at

indicators.note: being heard tells us the contraction is spoken aloud, not spelt

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of 'I would'

explanation.surface: Someone says briefly that they would be listened to and watched.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken contraction I'D sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or regard it closely, so eyed means looked at.

clue.text: Seat with front falling off — could this help fix it?

indicators.note: the word for seat loses its front, its first letter

parts.note: a stool is a seat without a back

explanation.surface: A broken seat whose front has come off, and a question about repairing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with front falling off' removes S from STOOL. The definition loops back to the surface: an implement could mend the broken stool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool, such as a screwdriver or hammer, is an implement used to repair things.

clue.text: A foreign fellow approaching, not the first character to be rude

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
a man is a fellow

indicators.note: not removes the following letter from the word for approaching

parts.note: nearly means approaching, as in nearly ten
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A rough foreign man coming towards you, unlike the main character, is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A from NEARLY, leaving NERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking good manners is impolite or discourteous, which is what rude means.

clue.text: Beastly home in Dorset town

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words Dorset town

explanation.surface: An animal's house in a town in the county of Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county in south-west England. The answer spans DorSET Town.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the burrow where badgers live, an animal's home.

clue.text: Pity — he nods off in a trance!

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of pity he nods are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pity that someone drops off to sleep as if entranced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hypnotised is held in a sleeplike state of suggestion, that is, entranced.
